blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A working tax calendar is much more than a list of deadlines. It is the spine of the finance team's year. Each deadline has an owner, a preparation window, a checklist, and a clear link to the internal process that feeds it. The owner knows what has to happen, when it has to happen, and what will go wrong if it does not.

Good calendars build in slack. VAT returns are ready three days before the legal deadline. Corporate tax is drafted a month before it is due. Payroll taxes run automatically from the salary system, with a manual check every month.

We are going to review the calendar every Monday this year — not to change it, but to see what is coming in the next two weeks and catch anything drifting. The routine is boring. The calm it produces is the whole point.

items.q: What does the text say a working tax calendar is?
options: The spine of the finance team's year
A monthly report to the board
items.why: "It is the spine of the finance team's year" — muito mais do que uma lista de prazos.

items.q: According to the text, when are VAT returns ready?
options: On the day they are due
Three days before the legal deadline
A month before they are due
items.why: "VAT returns are ready three days before the legal deadline." — a folga (slack) embutida.

items.q: What is the stated purpose of the Monday review?
options: To see what is coming and catch anything drifting
To rewrite the calendar each week
To assign new owners to deadlines
To report progress to the tax authority
items.why: "not to change it, but to see what is coming… and catch anything drifting."

items.q: The text says "The routine is boring. The calm it produces is the whole point." The author would most likely DISAGREE with…
options: Reliability matters more than drama in finance work
Boredom in this routine is acceptable if the result is calm
A predictable process is worth more than an exciting one here
Excitement in tax operations is a sign the system is working well
items.why: Inferência: o texto valoriza justamente o tédio previsível; empolgação sugeriria surpresas indesejadas.

items.q: The phrase "catch anything drifting" suggests that…
options: The calendar changes every week by design
Deadlines can quietly slip off track if no one watches
items.why: Inferência: 'drifting' indica prazos escapando aos poucos — a revisão semanal os pega cedo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily explicando a nova rotina de segunda-feira à equipe de finanças. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Morning, everyone. From this week, we are going to meet for fifteen minutes every Monday, right here, to look at the tax calendar together. It is short, it is calm, and I promise it will save us a lot of stress later in the year.

Here is how it will work. We will look two weeks ahead — never just the current week. Each deadline in that window has an owner, so when I read it out, that person tells us where they are. If VAT is due in ten days, I want to hear that the draft is already started, not that we will begin next week.

I am not going to change the calendar in these meetings. That is important. The dates stay as they are. What we are doing is catching anything that is drifting before it becomes a real problem. If a preparation window is slipping, we deal with it on the spot.

Payroll will keep running automatically from the salary system, but we will still do the manual check together on the first Monday of each month. Boring? Yes. But by December, you are going to thank me.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How often and for how long will the review meeting happen?
options: Once a month for half an hour
items.why: "we are going to meet for fifteen minutes every Monday."

items.q: How far ahead does Emily want the team to look?
items.why: "We will look two weeks ahead — never just the current week."

items.q: What does Emily explicitly say she will NOT do in these meetings?
items.why: "I am not going to change the calendar in these meetings… The dates stay as they are."

items.q: When Emily says she wants to hear "the draft is already started, not that we will begin next week", she is signalling that…
options: Drafts should be finished only after the deadline
She expects work to begin inside the preparation window, ahead of time
The team should wait until the last week to start
items.why: Inferência: ela quer trabalho já em andamento na janela de preparação, não deixado para depois.

items.q: How would you best describe Emily's overall message?
options: The team is failing and must be replaced
The calendar needs a complete redesign
The routine is dull but will pay off by year end
items.why: Inferência: "Boring? Yes. But by December, you are going to thank me." — tédio agora, calma depois.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The tax calendar is the spine of the finance team's year." Here, spine means…
options: the final deadline of the year
the central structure that everything else hangs on
items.why: Spine = espinha dorsal: a estrutura central que sustenta o resto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Good calendars build in ___, so returns are ready days before they are due, not on the day."
items.why: Slack = folga: a margem de tempo deixada de propósito.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Corporate tax is ___ a month before it is due, then reviewed before filing."
items.why: To draft = rascunhar; um primeiro rascunho é feito com antecedência.

items.q: A preparation window is best described as…
options: the person responsible for a deadline
the period set aside to get a task ready before it is due
items.why: Preparation window = janela de preparação: o intervalo reservado para deixar a tarefa pronta.

items.q: "Each deadline links to the internal process that feeds it." To feed a process means to…
options: supply it with the data or work it needs
items.why: To feed (a process) = alimentar: fornecer os dados/insumos de que ele precisa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem numa reunião de rotina financeira. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The controller still has to sign off on the VAT return before we file it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We are going to roll out the Monday review to every regional team next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "If a deadline is slipping, we deal with it on the spot." A deadline that is slipping is…
items.why: To slip = escorregar/atrasar: o prazo está ficando para trás sem alarde.

items.q: "The team agreed the plan but never followed through." This means they…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Skipping the manual check will not move the needle on speed, but it could cost us a fine." Move the needle means to…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
